SYMPTOM: k3s pod with hostPort stays Pending or Running but port not bound — old Docker container still holding the port
CAUSE: k3s uses containerd (not Docker) for port binding. hostPort in containerd doesn't steal ports from running Docker containers. Pod may show Running but port isn't actually bound if Docker still has it.
FIX:
  1. Stop Docker container first: docker stop <container>
  2. Then delete k3s pod: kubectl delete pod <pod>
  3. New pod starts and claims the hostPort
PREVENT: Always stop Docker containers on target ports before applying hostPort manifests. Verify with: ss -tlnp | grep <port>
